9.label: 9(a)
9.answer: The printed figures describe a cold continental climate with a warm summer, rather than true tundra: the warmest month is 19.4°C and five months reach at least 10°C.
9.explanation: A tundra climate has every monthly mean below 10°C. The Greenland label does not override the actual table.

9.label: 9(b)
9.answer: Very cold winters, a short much warmer summer, a large annual temperature range and modest precipitation with a summer maximum.
9.explanation: January is −18.9°C and July 19.4°C, giving a 38.3°C range.

9.label: 9(c)

10.label: 10 rotation
10.answer: Day/night; local time differences; apparent daily celestial motion; Coriolis deflection of winds and currents.

10.label: 10 revolution
10.answer: Seasonal changes in heating, changing day length, changing apparent overhead-Sun position and changing seasonal star visibility.
10.explanation: Annual orbit combined with axial tilt produces seasonal geometry.
